Alex —

Quick note attached: I put together a short summary and a checklist we can use in the kickoff. High level answers here, and I also included action items so the kickoff can be tactical.

Key bullets:
- Latency SLO: for 512-token average at 20 QPS we typically see 120–220ms p50 on a GPU-backed fp16 path; p95 depends on prefix caching and batching (can go up to ~600ms without batching controls).
- Batching: increases throughput and reduces per-token cost. To keep tail latency predictable we use dynamic batch caps + per-route latency SLOs. We recommend starting with a max batch size of 8 and target batch delay of 10–25ms for this workload.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated conversation roots gives the largest wins when >15% of tokens are reused across requests. We can enable prefix caching on a per-route basis; estimated cost reduction 12–35% depending on reuse.
- Quantization: recommend starting with GPU fp16 serving; progressive test of int8 quant profiles in a canary: qprofile-gpu-int8-s (lower memory, best for high throughput) and qprofile-gpu-int8-m (higher quality). If you need CPU routes, we can test per-customer signed-off CPU int8 but quality varies.
- Routing policies: policy examples provided: 1) latency-first (route to fp16 GPU; failover to int8 GPU), 2) cost-first (route to int8 GPU or burst to cheaper spot capacity), 3) hybrid schedule (business hours = latency-first; nights/weekends = cost-first). Policies are editable per-route in the Console.

Action items before kickoff:
1) Nimbus: share 48h sample of request traces (top prompts, seq len histogram, % streaming). Attached CSV template is helpful.
2) Redwood: prepare canary plan for quant profiles + suggested batch/delay settings.
3) Legal/Procurement: send any constraints on CPU-only acceptance.

Attach: redwood-kickoff-checklist.pdf, nimbus-onboard-telemetry-request.csv

See you on the call — Vanessa

Confirmed. I'll own the quant canary. High-level plan attached (short tech notes inline here):

- Models & qprofiles: test path = fp16 (baseline) -> qprofile-gpu-int8-s -> qprofile-gpu-int8-m. We'll also provide a low-priority CPU-int8 variant if Nimbus signs the CPU quality waiver.
- Memory/latency delta: expect ~25–40% memory reduction on int8-s vs fp16 and p50 token generation latency improvement ~10–20% at scale; p95 depends on batching and cache hit rate.
- Canary rollout: 0% (smoke) -> 5% (low QPS) -> 20% (load) -> 100%. Metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, token-cost-per-req, quality eval (BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy and human sample checks).
- Batch knobs: start: max_batch=8, target_delay_ms=15; emergency guardrails: per-request max_wait_ms=120.
- Cache: enable prefix caching for conversation roots; initial TTL 24h, with hit-rate telemetry in Console.

I'll attach the short canary doc to the HubSpot deal after Monica finalizes the cost delta numbers. Suggest an internal 30m sync Mon 11:00 PT to finalize.
